findings.claim: Only 2% of software-engineering papers (1993-2002) reported experiments; of those, 72.6% used students only as subjects. (Ch 1, "History of software engineering research")
findings.failure_mode: Two figures from different chapters fused and mis-cited. The 72.6% is a share of the 1.9% of papers reporting controlled experiments (Ch 13.1), not of the Ch 1 '2% reporting experiments'.
findings.evidence: Deep 15 and 272-273: 2% (Ch 1) vs 1.9% controlled experiments, of which 72.6% used students only (Ch 13.1). Source 10576 (Ch 1, 2%) and 41852-41854 (Ch 13.1, 1.9%, 72.6%).
findings.fix: correct: Only 2% of 5,453 software-engineering papers (1993-2002) reported experiments (Source: Ch 1, "History of software engineering research"); the same review, cited in Ch 13.1, found 1.9% reported controlled experiments, of which 72.6% used students only as subjects (Source: Ch 13.1, "Introduction").

findings.failure_mode: Wrong marker: the words are Goodhart's, which Jones relays; the deep ref marks [BT], and the distillation's own worked example (line 80) uses [BT].
findings.evidence: Deep 243: Goodhart quotation marked [BT]. Source 41870-41872: "Goodhart's law is an observation about human behavior, rather than a law: 'Any observed ...'"

findings.failure_mode: Verbatim re-extracted from the source rather than copied from the deep ref. The words match source 23685, but the deep ref carries only 'a speculative explanation' (unquoted) plus the quoted clause 'the two exponentials are driven by ...'.
findings.evidence: Deep 167; source 23685 "A speculative idea is that the two exponentials are driven by ..."
findings.fix: correct: Jones offers a speculative explanation: "the two exponentials are driven by the two independent processes that need to interact to produce a fault experience: the distribution of input values, and the mistakes contained in the source code" [V] (Source: Ch 6.3.1, "Input profile")

findings.claim: during an AAR it means many fault experiences trace to a small set of high-frequency input paths meeting a small set of concentrated mistakes
findings.failure_mode: Jones's explicitly speculative explanation is turned into what the pattern 'means', and the specific mechanism (small sets of high-frequency input paths meeting concentrated mistakes) is not in the deep ref.
findings.evidence: Deep 167: ranked duplicate-fault counts fit a bi-exponential; the two-process reading is 'speculative'. Nothing on 'high-frequency input paths' or 'concentrated mistakes'.
findings.fix: correct: during an AAR it suggests that some faults are experienced far more often than others, so the ranked profile of repeat fault experiences is worth drawing before remediation is scoped; Jones's two-process reading of why is speculative.

findings.claim: Agile-task data shows round-number anchoring — peaks at multiples of seven hours.
findings.failure_mode: Concept mislabelled and uncited. The deep ref presents the seven-hour peaks as round-number preference (Ch 5.3; Ch 2.7.1 'Numeric preferences'), a separate effect from anchoring (Ch 2.2.1). The sentence inherits the Ch 2.2.1 citation of the concept.
findings.evidence: Deep 145: Jones-and-Cullum 8,252 tasks, peaks at multiples of seven hours, 'round-number preferences influence development estimates' (Ch 5.3; Ch 2.7.1).
findings.fix: correct: Separately, agile-task data shows round-number preference, with estimate peaks at multiples of seven hours (Source: Ch 5.3, "Resource estimation"; Ch 2.7.1, "Numeric preferences").

findings.claim: Retraining investment is being scoped — What is this system's survival horizon? The survival-adjusted ROI calculation shapes how much it is worth investing in improvements.
findings.failure_mode: Framework stretched past its scope: the survival-rate-adjusted break-even applies to development-time investments that reduce the software's future maintenance cost, not to retraining people. Line 8's 'Phase 4 (retraining-resource allocation)' also misnames the task's Phase 4 (Action design).
findings.evidence: Deep 91: break-even ratio 'for development-time investments aimed at reducing future maintenance costs' incorporating system survival rate (Ch 3.2.3). Task spec tasks/aar.md: Phase 4 = Action design.
findings.fix: correct: Need 'A code or architecture improvement meant to cut future maintenance cost is being scoped'; keep the question.

findings.claim: Over 80% of coding mistakes never produce a fault experience
findings.failure_mode: Figure transferred to the wrong population. The >80% is for radiation-induced bit-flips (soft errors); the deep ref says only that 'many' coding mistakes never produce a fault experience.
findings.evidence: Deep 171 and 276: 'over 80% of bit-flips have no detectable impact on program behavior'; 'many coding mistakes never produce a fault experience'.
findings.fix: correct: Many coding mistakes never produce a fault experience (over 80% of injected bit-flips had no detectable effect); what threshold of risk reduction, not completeness, is the action targeting?

findings.claim: Private estimates before stakeholder reveal is the named response.
findings.failure_mode: Remedy attributed to the source ('the named response') that the deep ref does not contain. The deep ref documents anchoring effects (Jørgensen-Sjøberg; Aranda) but names no countermeasure.
findings.evidence: Deep 65, 145: anchoring findings only; no debiasing procedure.
findings.fix: strip the second sentence, or reword as the distillation's own suggestion without attributing it to Jones.

findings.claim: OB names the cognitive biases (confirmation bias, anchoring) that allow folklore to persist
findings.failure_mode: Claim about another source not in its deep ref: openstax-organizational-behavior-deep carries confirmation bias (Ch 6.4 barriers) but no anchoring.
findings.evidence: openstax-organizational-behavior-deep.md 189: confirmation bias among six barriers; grep for 'anchor' finds no anchoring-bias entry.
findings.fix: correct: OB names confirmation bias and the other Ch 6.4 decision barriers (bounded rationality, escalation of commitment) that let folklore persist

findings.claim: The anchoring finding (Jørgensen and Sjøberg) is cited borrowed-through in the deep ref (Ch 2.2.1)
findings.failure_mode: Misreports the deep ref's marker: the deep ref marks the finding [AP], not [BT]. The study is cited by Jones, so 'borrowed-through gap' is fair, but 'cited borrowed-through in the deep ref' is not.
findings.evidence: Deep 65: 'A study by Jørgensen and Sjøberg found ... [AP] (Ch 2.2.1)'.
findings.fix: correct: The anchoring finding (Jørgensen and Sjøberg) is a study Jones cites (deep ref marks it [AP], Ch 2.2.1); neither author is held directly in this corpus.

findings.claim: Brooks's Law is cited as a condition from Brooks's own work
findings.failure_mode: Attribution loosened: the law is Brooks's; the quantitative condition is the book's derivation in Ch 5.5.1 (citing Brooks 1995).
findings.evidence: Deep 99 and 293: 'Brooks's Law is presented quantitatively rather than as a maxim, with a derivation of the condition ...' (Ch 5.5.1, citing Brooks 1995).
findings.fix: correct: Brooks's Law comes from Brooks (1995), which the corpus does not hold; the quantitative condition is Jones's derivation (Ch 5.5.1).

findings.claim: The book explicitly does not cover real-time, embedded, or safety-critical software development as distinct domains with their own datasets. Its findings apply most directly to commercial software development contexts.
findings.failure_mode: Scope limit invented. The deep ref records no such exclusion and itself discusses embedded C software (Ch 7.2.7) and MC/DC coverage; the source discusses safety-critical systems repeatedly (e.g. 22541, 25163, 29610).
findings.fix: correct: The book's coverage is dictated by which public datasets exist, not by topic importance, which Jones says makes it 'a very patchy discussion' (Read me 1st).

findings.claim: The Goodhart's Law quotation is `[V]` in the deep ref; the distillation quotes it directly in Concept 2 with the `[V]` marker.
findings.failure_mode: Misstates the deep ref's marker, which is [BT]; the continuity note certifies the wrong marker.
findings.fix: correct: The Goodhart's Law quotation is `[BT]` in the deep ref (Jones relaying Goodhart); the distillation carries it as `[BT]` in Concept 2 and the worked example.

findings.claim: The anchoring finding is `[AP]` in the deep ref with `[BT]` to Jørgensen and Sjøberg
findings.fix: correct: The anchoring finding is `[AP]` in the deep ref (Jones summarising Jørgensen and Sjøberg).

notes: Quotations checked in the converted source: 'at best useless' (21602) and 'a mathematical artefact created by the choice of axis' (21616) are verbatim; 'closer to 0.8' (18217), '14:1 ... 6:1' (10701), 'net bias ...' (20772), 'little or no connection ...' (20648), McCabe 'accounting fraud' (24285-24287) all verbatim. The source says bidding decisions 'can be driven' by these factors; deep ref and distillation both drop 'can' (outside the quotation), noted not graded. The 'standard form contracts' finding is Marotta-Wurgler's study of 647 software licence agreements (source 20770-20772); applying it to vendor-client delivery contracts is the distillation's extension. Line 87 uses 'technical-debt remediation' as practitioner vocabulary; Jones rejects the term (deep 91), but the distillation does not attribute it to him. LFUO integration row's 'local-rationality' is not LFUO's term but the concept (decisions that made sense at the time) is in its deep ref (178), so graded faithful. Worked example is hypothetical and presents no outcome as a source finding.
